This message comes from Wealthfront.
Know you want to invest, but don't know where to start?
With a Wealthfront portfolio, it's easy.
Just answer a few questions, make a deposit, and you're set with a diversified strategy
that's designed to help you build wealth over time.
Get started at Wealthfront.com.
Investment management and advisory services provided by Wealthfront Advisors LLC, an SEC-registered
investment advisor.
Investing involves risk, including the possible loss of principal.
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
The Port of Seattle is asking federal officials whether immigration agents followed airport
protocol during an operation at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday.
Kate Stone from member station KUOW reports two passengers were arrested by ICE agents
on a packed jetway.
Witness video obtained by KUOW shows masked agents pulling two passengers out of the boarding
line for the Los Angeles-bound flight.
Security says ICE targeted Ricardo "Lorando" Mendoza and arrested Sofia Hernandez Meilla,
saying she threw hot coffee and will face a federal assault charge.
ICE says both are from Mexico and overstayed visas.
Major Aiden Mendoza, no relation, walked off the flight after watching what unfolded.
We want to help, but we're literally all trapped in this type of hallway, like we could get
her as well.
Alaska Airlines and the Port of Seattle say they were not notified.
Port officials are reviewing whether DHS breached airport protocols.
For NPR News, I'm Kate Stone in Seattle.
Officials in the San Francisco Bay area are preparing for Monster High King Tides after
being hit with heavy rain last week.
Brian Kranz from member station KQED reports the weather is being fueled by El Nino.
Some residents have already begun preparing for the worst.
In a muddy parking lot near the base shore, Joseph Abluhalawa filled up large white plastic
bags with sand and loaded them into the back of his pickup.
Definitely this year is probably the worst it's ever been.
Recent historic rainfall flooded his house in downtown Tiburon and Abluhalawa isn't sure
the sandbags can hold off the king tides.
I don't know, honestly, I'm just doing it to make myself feel better because the damage
is already pretty bad.
But it's going to make me feel at least more comfortable, like I'm doing something about
the problem.
The king tides are forecast to last three days, peaking Wednesday at seven feet high.
For NPR News, I'm Brian Kranz.
It's a short trading week on Wall Street, with investors watching holiday shopping and
home sales for clues about how much consumers are willing to spend.
NPR's Stephen Bissaha reports the Thanksgiving break follows a rough November for tech stocks.
Markets will be closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving, and tech companies might just be thankful for
one less trading day.
The tech-heavy NASDAQ has been consistently trending down in November.
The S&P 500, Dow, and the NASDAQ are now all in correction territory, meaning they are
down more than 10 percent from a recent high.
Wednesday, the U.S. Census Bureau will release sales data for new homes in October.
Trading home sales that month were down almost 9 percent from a year earlier.
And Thanksgiving weekend, an estimated 183 million shoppers will be hunting for holiday
deals, according to the National Retail Federation, about 2 percent lower than last year.
Stephen Bissaha, NPR News.
This is NPR.
Some Republicans in Congress say new Pentagon restrictions will have little effect on military
cooperation with Canada.
The limits were laid out in a classified memo from Defense Secretary Pete Hankseth.
They mainly affect which conferences and social events U.S. military officials can attend.
Scientists have discovered a tiny area in the brain that appears to act as a link between
hearing and speaking.
John Hamilton has more on the research in the journal Science.
It's called Wernicke's area, and for more than a century, it's been known as a place
where the brain processes incoming words.
But Dr. Eddie Chang of the University of California San Francisco says a study of 28 people found
Wernicke's area has another role.
In addition to the listening function, it also has a function for planning the words
that we're about to say next.
Just before a person speaks, a small group of neurons in Wernicke's area begin sending
signals that help organize the impending string of syllables.
The discovery of neurons involved in both input and output could help explain how children
learn to say the words they hear.
For NPR News, I'm John Hamilton.
Major League Baseball's Players' Union has rejected the league's proposal for an
international amateur draft.
The union wants to keep letting teams sign international prospects directly and give
clubs more money for signing bonuses.
The two sides are expected to resume contract talks tomorrow.
The current labor deal expires December 1, and team owners expect to lock out players
if there's no agreement.
This is NPR News in Washington.
